sections.title: A steady place to make sense of what you are carrying
paragraphs: Hi, I’m Amanda (she/her). I’m a **Registered Clinical Counsellor** (license #29097) with the BC Association of Clinical Counsellors.

While my counselling work currently focuses on eating disorder recovery and disordered eating, including anorexia, bulimia, orthorexia, binge eating, and body image concerns, I also welcome clients who may be looking for support with anxiety, depression, life transitions, self-worth, and burnout.

Early on in my undergraduate degree, I had the pleasure of meeting people in eating disorder recovery. They shared their stories with me, describing the isolation and stigma they felt and the lack of resources available to help them in their recovery.

Hearing their stories and witnessing their resilience and vulnerability inspired me to volunteer with a local non-profit, **Looking Glass Foundation**, to help increase access to mental health support for those in eating disorder recovery. I deeply cherished my time there, so I returned as a practicum student during my graduate program to deepen my skill set.

I am truly passionate about this work. I have seen people make incredible strides in their recovery, from it completely ruling their life to thriving and leading lives aligned with who they are at their core, not the eating disorder. They have shown me and others that **recovery is possible**.

When I'm not counselling, you'll find me supporting youth with learning differences in developing their literacy skills, discovering new music, attending concerts, going for long walks by the ocean, connecting (and usually laughing) with loved ones, and improving my watercolour skills.

sections.title: My Approach
paragraphs: Because I believe that no two healing journeys are the same, I meet clients where they are and honour their individual pace, needs, and capacity throughout the counselling process. I take a **collaborative**, **holistic**, and **trauma-informed** approach to counselling, striving to meet each person with warmth, empathy, non-judgement, and a desire to truly understand their unique experiences. Clients have shared that they also appreciate my authenticity (I am not a
counsellor - I will bring my humanness into the room), playfulness, and willingness to help them stay accountable throughout our work together.

Through my own experience as a counselling client, I know how important it is to find a counsellor who feels like the right fit for **you**, where you feel safe, respected, and supported. With the right match, you can truly transform your life.

sections.title: Modalities
paragraphs: My work is integrative, blending mind-body therapeutic approaches with a particular focus on attachment and the impact of early experiences on our development, and how those experiences may still be impacting our mental wellness in adulthood. Together, we can explore the approaches and strategies that feel most supportive and aligned for you, tailoring counselling to your unique needs.

The therapeutic approaches I typically draw from include:

- Accelerated Experiential Dynamic Psychotherapy (AEDP)
- Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
- Compassion-Focused Therapy
- Internal Family Systems (IFS)
- Motivational Interviewing
- Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT)
- Mindfulness
- Psychodynamic approaches

sections.title: How we work together
sections.description: Counselling here is collaborative and practical, drawing on **person-centred**, **trauma-informed**, and **mind-body** approaches that fit your goals.

items.title: Collaborative care
items.description: Counselling works best when goals, pace, and focus are shaped together, and I encourage you to let me know what works and what does not.

items.title: Respect for lived experience
items.description: You're the **expert** in your own life. You bring wisdom about your experiences, identities, relationships, and needs.

items.title: Practical support
items.description:
Sessions can include:

- reflection
- skill-building
- nervous system support
- clear next steps
